ibkrApi.guideToggle: How to create a Flex Query and get your token →
ibkrApi.guideIntro: You need two things: a Token (account-level key, generated once) and a Query ID (from a Flex Query you create). Both live in the same section of the Client Portal.
ibkrApi.step1Title: Step 1 — Log in to the IBKR Client Portal
ibkrApi.step1Body: Go to clientportal.ibkr.com and sign in with your IBKR credentials.
ibkrApi.step2Body: Click Performance & Reports in the top menu, then select Flex Queries. Alternatively, click the hamburger menu (top left) → Reporting → Flex Queries.
ibkrApi.step3Intro: On the Flex Queries page, find the Flex Web Service Configuration section (usually on the right side or accessible via a gear/configure icon). Then:
ibkrApi.step3Item1: Enable the Flex Web Service by toggling it on and clicking Save
ibkrApi.step3Item3: Choose an expiration period (select 1 year so it doesn't expire during tax season)
ibkrApi.step3Item4: Copy the token string that appears — paste it in the Flex Query Token field above
ibkrApi.step3Note: The token is account-wide and works for all your queries. Generating a new one invalidates the previous one.
ibkrApi.step4Title: Step 4 — Create a new Activity Flex Query
ibkrApi.step4Body: Back on the Flex Queries page, click the + icon next to Activity Flex Query. Give it a name like IB-Taxil {year}.
ibkrApi.step5Intro: Enable only these two sections (leave everything else unchecked):
ibkrApi.step5Item2: Cash Transactions — dividends and withholding tax
ibkrApi.step5Note: Inside Cash Transactions, make sure Dividends and Withholding Tax sub-types are both checked.
ibkrApi.step6Warning: Note on date range: The Client Portal does not offer a "specific calendar year" option. Last 365 Calendar Days is the closest available — it works well if you're filing shortly after year-end (January–March). If you need exactly Jan 1–Dec 31 {year}, use the file upload option instead: download the report manually from the portal (where you can filter by exact dates) and drop it in the Upload card.
ibkrApi.step7Title: Step 7 — Save and find the Query ID
ibkrApi.step7Body: Click Create (or Save). The query appears in the list. Click on it to open it — the Query ID is the numeric code shown in the query details (e.g. 123456). Copy it into the Query ID field above.
ibkrApi.securityTip: Security tip: The token is read-only — it cannot place trades or move money. Once you've finished generating your tax report, consider regenerating the token in IBKR to invalidate the old one.

privacyModal.title: How your data is protected
privacyModal.subtitle: Plain-language explanation — no technical jargon.
privacyModal.section1Title: What is a Flex Query token?
privacyModal.section1Body: A Flex Query token is a read-only key that IBKR generates for you. It can only download reports from your account. It cannot place trades, withdraw money, or change any settings. Think of it as a key that only opens the filing cabinet — it cannot touch the cash register.
privacyModal.section2Body: We only request your trade history, dividend payments, and withholding taxes for the selected tax year. Nothing else is requested or downloaded.
privacyModal.section3Body: Your data goes from IBKR directly into your browser's memory. It never touches our servers in a form we can read, log, or store. The moment you close this tab, all data is gone.
privacyModal.section4Body: Your browser cannot call IBKR directly due to a web security restriction called CORS. We use a tiny relay (called a proxy) that forwards your request to IBKR and sends the response back to your browser. The relay does not log, store, or read the content — it is a dumb pipe. The code is open source and publicly auditable.
privacyModal.section5Item1: Store your token or financial data on any server
privacyModal.section5Item3: Share or sell data to any third party
privacyModal.section5Item4: Use your data for anything other than generating your tax summary
privacyModal.section6Title: How do I revoke the token?
privacyModal.section6Body: Log in to IBKR → Account Management → Reports → Flex Queries → Delete the query token at any time. We recommend doing this after you've generated your tax report.

flexGuide.toggle: 📄 How to create & download your Flex Query (full walkthrough) →
flexGuide.intro: IBKR has two kinds of reports. An Activity Statement looks complete, but it does not include the per-lot purchase date and cost that Israeli capital-gains tax needs. You need an Activity Flex Query, exported as XML. It takes about five minutes to set up once, and the same query can be reused every year.
flexGuide.criticalTitle: Three settings that must be exactly right
flexGuide.critical1: Trades section → Options → Level of Detail = Closed Lots. This is what carries each sale’s original purchase date and cost. Without it, capital gains cannot be calculated and the file is rejected.
flexGuide.critical2: Delivery/General Configuration → Format = XML (not CSV, not the on-screen default). Only XML can be read here.
flexGuide.critical3: When you run the query, set the period to a Custom Date Range of Jan 1 – Dec 31 {year}. Getting the exact tax year is the main reason to upload a file instead of using the API.
flexGuide.step1Title: 1. Log in to the Client Portal
flexGuide.step1Body: On a desktop browser, go to interactivebrokers.com and log in to the Client Portal (Account Management). The mobile app cannot build Flex Queries.
flexGuide.step2Body: Click the menu (☰), then Performance & Reports → Flex Queries. If you can’t find it, type “Flex Queries” in the portal search box at the top.
flexGuide.step3Title: 3. Create a new Activity Flex Query
flexGuide.step3Body: Next to “Activity Flex Query”, click the + (Configure/Create) button. Name it something like “IB-Taxil {year}”. Keep it an Activity Flex Query — do not use the Trade Confirmation Flex Query.
flexGuide.step4Title: 4. Add the Trades section — with Closed Lots
flexGuide.step4Body: Open Sections → Trades. In the panel that appears:
flexGuide.step4Item1: Under Options → Level of Detail, tick Closed Lots. You can leave Execution and Orders unticked.
flexGuide.step4Item2: For the fields/columns, the simplest safe choice is Select All — the tool reads only what it needs and ignores everything else.
flexGuide.step4Item3: Click Save to return to the sections list.
flexGuide.step5Title: 5. Add the Cash Transactions section — income & tax withheld
flexGuide.step5Body: Back in Sections, open Cash Transactions. Enable these sub-types (each is a checkbox), choose Select All for the fields, and Save:
flexGuide.step5Item2: Payment In Lieu Of Dividends — taxed the same as dividends; include it so nothing is missed.
flexGuide.step5Item3: Withholding Tax — the foreign (e.g. US) tax already deducted; this feeds your foreign-tax credit.
flexGuide.step5Item4: Broker Interest Received — interest paid to you. Only needed if you earned interest.
flexGuide.step6Title: 6. Set the format, date format and period
flexGuide.step6Body: Scroll to General / Delivery Configuration and set:
flexGuide.step6Item3: Period: Custom Date Range, so you can pick exact dates each time you run it (Jan 1 – Dec 31 {year}).
flexGuide.step6Item4: Include Canceled Trades?: No. Leave the other options at their defaults.
flexGuide.step7Body: Click Continue, review the summary, then Create. Your query now appears in the Activity Flex Query list.
flexGuide.step8Title: 8. Run it and download the XML
flexGuide.step8Body: Click the Run (▶) icon next to your query. When prompted, choose the Custom Date Range Jan 1 – Dec 31 {year} and format XML, then Run. Your browser downloads a .xml file.
flexGuide.step9Body: Drag that .xml file into the box above (or click to browse). It is processed entirely in your browser — the file never leaves your device.
flexGuide.trouble1: “This looks like an Activity Statement” — you downloaded a Statement instead of a Flex Query. Return to Flex Queries and run the query you built above.
flexGuide.trouble2: “Missing closed-lot detail” or capital gains are absent — the Trades section wasn’t set to Closed Lots. Edit the query (step 4), fix it, save, and download again.
flexGuide.trouble3: Wrong year or partial data — re-run the query with the Custom Date Range set to exactly Jan 1 – Dec 31 {year}.
flexGuide.note: The Flex Query report is read-only: it contains no login credentials and cannot trade or move money. You can delete the downloaded file after uploading it.

step4Details.title: A couple of optional details
step4Details.subtitle: These help refine your result. Skip either one if it doesn’t apply.
step4Details.broughtForwardHelp: If a previous tax return recorded a capital loss you haven’t used yet, enter the shekel amount. It offsets this year’s capital gains only. Leave blank if none.
step4Details.otherIncomeHelp: Your salary and any other annual taxable income, in shekels. Used only to check the high-income surtax (מס יסף). Leave blank to skip the surtax check.
